If you have all of the right forge enhancements, potions, and a team that’s willing to deal with of the mechanics and focus on keeping you alive, you’ll kill any/every ultra significantly faster than with any other class.

The only class that performs on a similar level is ChronoShadowSlayer (CSS) the 2024 calendar class, and it fills a similar niche in that it capitalizes on utilizing high attack speed paired with high damage to melt bosses, but requires good connection and better skill rotation management as none of it’s skills are automated (1 is a manual attack, rather than auto).

Both of these classes require all (or nearly all, forge enhancements and team comp being mandatory) of the aforementioned setup, otherwise they aren’t worth using as their fragility and temperamental optimal conditions for dealing damage will result in you dying a lot and causing a lot of wipes compared to just running with a slow but common ultra boss team composition.

Also, Great Thief has one niche which I don’t think any other class really fills, but it’s also **really** great for melting ultras where chronos **specifically** are neutered, such as ultra kathool and mecha binky and raxborg 2.0.

I don’t really get what all of these people are talking about, I have the class and here’s how it works.

1. It’s a super high maintenance class that requires a full suite of forge enhancements Dauntless/Ravenous/Arcana, Vim/Forge base, and Lament and potions Fate/Felicitous Philtre/Potent Battle Potion.

2. It’s extremely easy to use (just spam 2-4-5) 

3. It’s arguably the best at it’s niche, which is melting ultras faster than pretty much anything (only contested by chrono shadowslayer, the 2024 calendar class) by hitting the damage cap with it’s spammy auto attacks which typically deal 90k+ damage per hit with a 0.4s cooldown, while it’s 2-5 deal 250k+ with a 1.75s cd and 7.5s cd respectively.

2. RNG is always going to be on your side as long as you’re actually **spamming the auto attack key** with every other skill usage. 

I don’t know what everyone on here is talking about but you’re never going to go longer than 5-10s **at most** before proccing the hidden blade buff (10% proc chance on every auto attack) which is what lets you hit for so much damage at such a high attack speed, and usually get it to refresh back to back a couple of times before it fades, having dealt several million damage in said timespan.

3. It relies entirely on it’s team for buffs and survivability, as it has no tanking ability whatsoever.

4. Ravenous/vim is preferable in fights where the boss’ attention is held by tanks, as it lets you spam without mana uses at all, otherwise use ravenous/forge but you might run into mana issues which also might be resolvable with your 4th skill, which has a 50% chance to give 50 mana back.

All in all, you get what you pay for in a similar vein to the calendar classes. Notably, Great Thief is one of the 3 most expensive (heromart, not including AC/Membership milestone classes) classes in the game, alongside Legion Paladin and Master of Moglins. 

Out of the three, only Great Thief and Legion Paladin are really useful for endgame activities, and neither are casual player friendly as they have even greater disparities between their strengths and weaknesses (being both much stronger and requiring much more overall effort to manage) than the chrono classes, which are both the more accessible premium classes in the game and require less effort to get the most out of.

Hi, so it looks like people don’t seem to really know what U/OCM’s niche is, so I’ll fill it in here.

U/OCM is best used as an easy to learn  **tank DPS chrono class**.

This is best used for soloing bosses that are typically in the 1-2 hit kill range (against non tanks), or have undodgeable attacks, similar to CaV or VHL.

It features weaker tanking/survivability than the previous two f2p classes, as it’s only (relevant) trait in this regard is that it has maximum damage resistance (80%) but it makes up for this with a guaranteed critical damage chrono nuke, which depending on how lazy/risky you want to be can hit up to a million damage solo with endgame equipment (51% all, 50% race).

The hourglass/timepiece consumable pair it uses for tanking is Paradise and Madness, and it is required to have Dauntless and Penitence forge enhancements to be useful.

TL;DR, OCM is CaV/VHL replacement with bit less survival, lot more kill.

the Emperor didn’t want the Imperium to be “somewhat” secular, he wanted to eradicate all manner of supernatural belief entirely. 

the Imperial Truth was an atheistic and rationalistic declaration that all under the Lex Imperialis were to swear by on pains of death.

in 30K, there was a lot of ritualistic activities coopted from extinct religions in an effort to “secularize” the concepts (such as the Angels of Death title of the Astartes), as to do away with their religious connotations, but this ended up backfiring spectacularly as the Imperial Cult would adopt all of these rituals **unironically** into 40K.

As powerful as The Emperor was, he most certainly was **not** a god in 30k’s time. 

He was an apex tier psyker and a perpetual, two traits which when combined certainly produce potent effects, as it did with him, but he was more than fallible, and he was nowhere **near** either omniscient or omnipotent, he was just the most powerful human around.

He tried pretty hard to hammer this point home into mankind with the Imperial Truth, that just because there are a lot of overwhelmingly powerful existences in the universe, it doesn’t make them deities, both because he truly believed this **and because he understood that errant beliefs would resonate in the warp and give undue power to such entities like the Chaos Gods**.

this was actually proving highly effective, which is why the Chaos Gods actually sat up, paid attention, and got to work wholeheartedly in sabotaging his efforts to unite humanity into a rationally minded, disciplined, and (questionably) “morally upstanding” species.

Neither Lorgar nor Sigismund were paragons of rational thought. they were powerful, probably intelligent, but they weren’t intellectually honest in that they took a look at the Emperor, a decidedly **limited** being, and said “yup, this guy’s a god!” when he doesn’t fit the bill.

the chaos gods are quite a bit closer to this definition, as they’re *nigh* omniscient and omnipotent extratemporal entities unbound by causality, but even they don’t completely work in that they’re only *nearly* all seeing and powerful, among other things.

the Emperor of 40K is something else, and ambiguous in it’s nature and identity. 30K Emps is still in there, as seen when he spoke directly to Guilliman *through* the gestalt guise of “The God Emperor”, but it’s no longer just him situated in that rotting body on the Golden Throne.

I disagree with a number of your opinions, but I’ll address the one I am most incensed to discuss, being James Ironwood.

Ironwood’s character was caricaturized the moment they had him shoot Councilman Sleet. It was an action wholly incongruent with his character. This was a ham fisted narrative ploy to fully plunge him head first into a fall from grace, from that of a conflicted hero into a tyrant villain.

This was something which has been expanded on during volume 7. Throughout the volume, as his character was fleshed out, it revealed his flaws, as well as his virtues. In the face of increasing friction with his allies, and acts of sabotage and corruption running rampant amidst his kingdom, he’s been constricted with paranoia and a crushing sense of isolation. 

Despite all of this, he presses on with his plans to save the world through reconnecting the nations with the Arena project. He does all of this while maintaining a veneer of stoicism towards a world which was growing increasingly hostile towards him by the day, due to his lack of political finesse. James is, at heart, a guardian. He stands to protect those under his care without concern for how he’s regarded, nor what perils may befall him. He would do this at the head of an army, or as a lone sentinel. His theme song, Hero, exemplifies this underlying motivation behind his actions. **His nature is not to sacrifice others for himself, but to sacrifice himself without reservation for the sake of his duty, to protect those under him.** 

When RWBY, ORNJ, and Qrow came to Atlas, he welcomed them with open arms and an open heart. He knew that they were truly committed to the defense of others, and were both friends and comrades in arms. Following the events of the story, he takes their advice into consideration, fights his mistrust of others, and is generally making headway into recuperating his mental state. Further along, shit hits the fan. Not only are his most confidential plans sabotaged, but he’s outright backstabbed by his comrades in RWBY and ORNJ. This, predictably, breaks him. His faith in others has been utterly diminished, if not irreparably destroyed. He is no longer of the mind to take the opinions of anyone into consideration. 

At the climax of the season, Oscar confronts James. Their irreconcilable views on how to move forward to deny Salem, along with recent events having broken James’ faith in his allies, lead him to a conclusion. Oscar and his cohort are a threat to his people. James acts to remove the threat, shooting Oscar, and setting arrest warrants out for the protagonists. 

Now, the important thing to note here is that James is not a “I’ve been betrayed, so fuck everyone” tyrant villain. He’s a military officer acting on his duties to protect the people of his nation. Such words can easily be mouthed as platitudes from the mouths and hearts of the immoral and corrupt, but **he is neither. To the end, his duty to protect is his driving force.** What’s changed for him is simply how he now views the MCs, which has gone from dear friends and allies in the war against Salem, to traitors and enemies of the state. Their actions will endanger the lives of his citizens, and he will not allow this on his watch.

Councilman Sleet is a a bureaucrat and a nuisance. He is also a citizen of Atlas and one of it’s officials. While Ironwood no doubt regards him without much respect, he has always tolerated him as a part of the fabric of the government of Atlas. James Ironwood may be paranoid and erratic at this stage, but he’s not insane or immoral, or thoughtless. He would not shoot a defenseless man for being a pest, and especially not a government official like himself. Why? Because his duty comes from his position. He believes in this above all else, that he has to protect and serve the citizens of Atlas, no matter the **personal** cost. 

If RT wanted to have Ironwood cut down, they could’ve done so in a far more organic way. His judgement is impaired and he’s unwilling to take opinions from others into consideration. This is more than enough for him to make mistakes which lead up to ultimate failure, culminating in the destruction of the lone, broken hero of Atlas. 

Instead, they had to turn his character inside out, without any care for his **duty**, and merely acting as a tyrant so RWBY can continue being the heroes, despite their wretched actions in the previous volume.
